header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH AT KARACHI
DATE ORDER WITH SIGNATURE OF JUDGE
Mr. Syed Muhammad Nabeel Mustafa, Advocate, along with the Petitioner.
Respondent No.1 Sajeel Ahmad, in person.
Mr. Sahriq Mubashir learned Assistant Advocate General
body: MUHAMMAD HASAN (AKBER), J.- The Judgement dated 08.08.2025 [impugned Judgment] has been assailed in this petition, passed in Guardian and Wards Appeal No.23/2025 ‘Falak Salim versus Shajeel Ahmad’, by learned VI Additional District Judge Karachi Central, modifying the Order dated 17.05.2024 passed by the learned XVI Family Judge Karachi Central, in G&W Application No.2611/2020 ‘Sajeel Ahmad vs. Falak Saleem’ [impugned Order].
2. Heard the parties in person, the learned counsel and the learned AAG and perused the record. Their respective contentions are considered and recorded at the relevant portions of this Order.

3. The petition concerns baby ‘Mirha Sajeel’ [Ward], a female aged about 6 to 7 years, permanently living with her petitioner [Mother]. For her permanent custody, the Respondent [Father], initiated Guardian and Wards Application No.2611/2020, ‘Sajeel Ahmad vs. Falak Saleem’ under section 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act 1890 [Act 1890], which was dismissed vide Order dated 22.02.2023, which was not assailed by either party, and the same has attained Finality. In the said Order, a meeting schedule was allowed between the ward and the Father, which was being followed.

4. Subsequently, the Father filed an application seeking modification/ variation in the visitation/temporary custody hours with the Ward, for increase in the visitation hours and for overnight stay of the Ward with him on weekends. The application was allowed vide impugned Order dated 17.05.2025, and the visitation schedule, which was earlier fixed from 12 pm to 5 pm on alternate Saturdays, was modified in the terms that overnight meetings on two weekends of the month were allowed. Meetings on both Eids were also allowed, whereas other terms were ordered to remain the same, subject to a fresh PR bond in the sum of Rs.1 million by the Father.

5. The Order was assailed by the Mother in G&W Appeal No.23/2025 which was disposed of vide the impugned Judgement in the terms that meetings from 10 am to 6 pm on each and every Sunday were allowed, and meetings on both Eids from 12 noon on the second day of eight till 12 noon of the third day of Eid were allowed, whereas all other terms were ordered to remain the same. Albeit the said Order has not been assailed by the Respondent side, nevertheless the Mother has challenged it in this petition.

6. As is apparent from the above narration, the permanent custody of the Ward has already been ordered to permanently remain with the Mother, which has not been assailed by the Father before any forum, and the same has attained Finality. The visitation rights which were allowed in the same Order were requested to be altered by the Father, and both the Courts below have dealt with the same differently, with certain variations in the meeting schedule.

7. During the course of hearing, the issue of payment of maintenance of the Ward was also argued, and both sides filed their respective Statements and calculations, to show the expenses incurred and payments made with respect to the Ward by the Father. Perusal of the statements and calculations based upon 10% annual increment as was allowed by the learned trial Court reflects that from October 2020 a large portion of the amounts have already been paid by the father. The Father undertakes to this Court to clear all outstanding amounts within 30 days of this Order and the continue to pay regularly.

8. As regards the meeting schedule, both sides, after arguing the matter at length, and after considering the gender and age of the Ward and also after considering the meeting schedules allowed by this Court in numerous other cases with identical facts, jointly submit that they would be satisfied if the instant petition is disposed of, in terms of the following Comprehensive Meeting Schedule between the Ward and the Father, by consent of the parties:
i. Custody: the permanent custody of the Ward shall remain with the Mother, with permission to travel within Pakistan on vacations, etc.

ii. Regular Meetings: Every 1 st and 3 rd Sundays and 2 nd and 4 th Saturdays of each month; From 10:00 am to 6:00 pm; at the residence of the Father; for which pick-and-drop from and to the Mother’s residence, shall be conducted by the Father.
iii. Ward's Birthday: from 4 pm to 7 pm at Father’s place.
iv. Father's Birthday: from 4 pm to 7 pm at Father’s place.
v. Eid-ul-Fitr: 2 nd day of Eid from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm.
vi. Eid-ul-Azha: 2 nd day of Eid from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm.
vii. Summer vacations: same as at clause (ii) above, OR as may be further agreed between the parties and the Ward.
viii. Winter vacations: same as at clause (ii) above, OR as may be further agreed between the parties and the Ward.
ix. Venue: All Meetings to be conducted at Father’s residence.
x. Meeting Costs: nil.
xi. Maintenance: Father shall continue to deposit monthly maintenance as already ordered by the Family Court.
xii. Security: Father shall furnish with the learned Family Court a fresh P.R Bond in the sum of Rs.10,00,000/- [Rupees one million] for compliance with the terms and conditions of this Order.

xiii. Exceptions: Notwithstanding the above schedule, the meeting arrangements shall be implemented strictly considering the health and education of each Ward, and in case of any difficulty, subject to the ruling by the learned Guardian Court.

xiv. Alterations: The above days, timings, venue or occasions etc. can be altered only with the express mutual consent of the Ward and both parents. xv. Education: (a) Mother may be at liberty to look after the health and education of the Ward, in the school(s) of her choice and other day-to-day needs of the Ward. (b) Annual reports regarding educational status/ results of the Ward be submitted by the Mother before the Family Court. (c) Both parents may attend important school meetings, other school functions, or any other activity of the Ward, as required, only to improve the confidence, better personality and education of the Ward. NOTE: Parents must avoid creating any embarrassing situation for the Ward during such meetings.
xvi. Gifts: Gifts from the Father, if any, be delivered to the Ward personally or through the learned Family Court.

xvii. Mutual Cooperation: In the best interests of the Ward, both parents shall fully cooperate with each other on all matters and documentation(s), etc., as, when and wherever required by the Ward's education institution, NADRA, Union Council, Immigration, Passports or any forum/ Department/ authority etc. and in this regard, the learned Family Court may pass appropriate Orders for its strict implementation.

xviii. Implementation: For implementation of this Order, as well as for all matters and guidance concerning the rights and welfare of the Ward, the parties shall approach the concerned learned Family Court.
xix. Action: The learned Family Judge may take action against the noncooperating party for non-compliance or any deliberate avoidance of the terms of this consent Order.
xx. Court: wherever used in this Order, shall mean the concerned Family Court which passed the decree. The learned Family Court may make further Orders in the best interests of the Ward.

9. Order accordingly, and the impugned Judgment and Order are therefore modified by consent; and in terms of the above Comprehensive Meetings Schedule of visitations/meetings between the Ward and the Father, reached by consent of the parties, is made the Order of the Court.
The instant petition is disposed of in the above terms, along with pending applications.
JUDGE
